notes: These are four competing replacements for the SAME RM13,491 total; never add basket totals together.
The existing funded mandate and historical holdings remain unchanged. Current Rakuten positions, buying power, FX and product availability must be verified first.
Cash is a liquidity reserve, not a mathematical hedge. Negative illustrations are not maximum losses.
Illustrative company/ETF returns are deliberately assumed sensitivities rather than issuer-derived forecasts; exclude fees, FX, dividends and taxes.

groups.label: Two catalysts
groups.subtitle: Two distinct earnings or repricing engines.

groups.label: Geopolitical supply
groups.subtitle: A conditional oil supply disruption expression.

baskets.name: Dry-powder optionality
baskets.risk: Lower market exposure, but not capital-protected
baskets.why: Build exposure to uranium re-rating and nitrogen profits while retaining cash for better entries.
baskets.whatCanGoWrong: Uranium can keep selling off; cash earns no return in this illustration, and MYR purchasing power can erode.
baskets.reconsider: CF's post-Q3 earnings weaken, uranium prices/contracting deteriorate, or existing holdings already consume the risk budget.
baskets.check: Verify all account holdings, URNM eligibility and after-earnings CF valuation.

baskets.name: Nuclear + nitrogen
baskets.why: Combine uranium miners' possible equity repricing with CF's nitrogen earnings exposure.
baskets.whatCanGoWrong: Both positions can fall together in credit tightening or broad risk-off; nitrogen margins may narrow if input costs rise.
baskets.reconsider: URNM sells off for fundamental reasons, CF profit quality weakens or ETF + producer overlap exceeds the funding budget.
baskets.check: Review uranium miners' contract economics, CF Q3, real portfolio energy exposure and USD/MYR.

baskets.name: Oil + fertiliser
baskets.why: Express higher-for-longer crude and a nitrogen margin opportunity, without owning many oil producers.
baskets.whatCanGoWrong: A durable supply recovery may compress the oil premium; higher gas input costs can hurt CF. Existing XOM/energy exposure creates overlap.
baskets.reconsider: EIA's Brent normalisation path becomes more likely, or current holdings already exceed intended energy limits.
baskets.check: First reconcile existing XOM, MISC, HIBISCS and DAYANG holdings; then review crude/forward margins and CF results.

baskets.name: Uranium repricing
baskets.why: Make the miner/uranium commodity divergence the main bet instead of diversifying away the thesis.
baskets.whatCanGoWrong: Mine economics, equity valuations or physical uranium can fall; 45% cash does not prevent large NAV drawdowns.
baskets.reconsider: Spot/term uranium signals weaken or the miners' equity decline reflects structural rather than temporary issues.
baskets.check: Validate URNM holdings and current market price, broker access, conversion costs and tolerance for >20% NAV drawdowns.
